posts.title: Reproducible gzip output, Python 3.11-3.15
posts.description: I noticed that in a project of mine a gzip output was not reproducible. Initially I saw that it was larger in Python 3.15 than earlier versions, but it turns out that there were other differences as well. Based on the very good list of changes in the python.org documentation for gzip.compress , I could reverse engineer what was necessary to get a reproducible gzip output across all versions of int

posts.title: A one-liner to copy an image to clipboard on Linux
posts.description: This uses the standard xclip program (debian package: xclip) and graphicsmagic (debian package: graphicsmagick-imagemagick-compat) to convert most any kind of image to one that can be pasted into programs that accept images. #!/bin/sh convert "$1" png:- | xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -i
